# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly, over seventy years old  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c35 P14](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0014)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012)</sub>
- **Status:** Widow  <sub>[v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012), [v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper for college students  <sub>[v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a little, softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and large, soft blue eyes filled with youth and hope. She has thick, snow-white hair, which she wears in quaint little puffs over her ears. She dresses in an old-fashioned style, often seen wrapped in a shawl and holding a cat or knitting.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c19 P0](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0000)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina possesses an exceptionally youthful, mirthful, and hopeful spirit that belies her advanced years. She is warm-hearted, kind, and deeply devout, while simultaneously holding a cheerful, pragmatic philosophy toward life's worries. Although she holds firm, old-fashioned morals, she has a lively sense of humor and a great capacity for indulgently loving the young people around her.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P63](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0063), [v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 c37 P19](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0019)_

- Warm-hearted  <sub>[v3 c16 P43](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0043)</sub>
- Cheerful and humorous  <sub>[v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 c37 P19](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0019)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c19 P0](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0000)</sub>

## Goals

- To provide a warm, comfortable home for her student charges at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina, an elderly widow whose only daughter Elizabeth left to become a missionary in India, agreed to move to Kingsport to act as housekeeper and chaperon for her grand-niece Stella Maynard and her friends Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. Bringing her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, she quickly won the deep love and admiration of the girls through her indulgent, mirthful nature and practical wisdom. She chose to remain at Patty's Place over the Christmas holidays to care for the cats, including Anne's adopted stray cat, Rusty. She successfully ran the household for two years during the girls' time at Redmond College, offering them sound life advice, comforting humor, and motherly care. After the girls graduated, she adopted all three cats and returned to her home, later visiting India to see her daughter.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c35 P8](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0008), [v3 c37 P17](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0017)_

## Background by volume

- Was named Jamesina because her father, James, was drowned at sea a month before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012)</sub>
- Had a daughter named Elizabeth who became an M.A. and went to India as a foreign missionary  <sub>[v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c30 P16](../source/v03-c30.md#nw-v03-c30-p0016)</sub>
- Was left alone in a large house after her daughter's departure before agreeing to manage Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P12](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0012)</sub>

## Quotes

> New shoes are smarter than old ones, but the old ones are more comfortable. I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> I know you expect me to look after you and keep you proper, but I’m not going to do it. You’re old enough to know how to behave if you’re ever going to be. So, as far as I am concerned, you can all go to destruction in your own way.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> The teens are such a nice part of life. I’m glad I’ve never gone out of them myself.  <sub>[v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P3](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0003)</sub>

> When you’ve learned to laugh at the things that should be laughed at, and not to laugh at those that shouldn’t, you’ve got wisdom and understanding.  <sub>[v3 c37 P19](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0019)</sub>
